svg.title: A 25-year-old man with a 3-year history of HIV is admitted to the medical-surgical unit with respiratory distress. 1100. A 25-year-old man who has been HIV positive for 3 years is admitted with a dry cough and a fever of 38.3°C (101.0°F). He has fatigue and shortness of breath, a respiratory rate of 28/min and an SpO₂ of 90% on room air . Breathing is slightly labored and his chest feels tight on a deep breath. He has taken antiretroviral medication since diagnosis but stopped it recently when he was laid off from his job . Three days of over-the-counter medication did not help. IV 0.9% sodium chloride is infusing in the right arm at 75 mL/hr. Labs drawn. Bronchoalveolar lavage completed, cytology pending.
svg.desc: This case walks the whole clinical judgment model in order — recognize the cues, analyze them, prioritize, generate solutions, take action, evaluate — and every step turns on the same fact: he stopped his antiretroviral medication when he lost his job. That is the risk factor, the reason the CD4 count has collapsed, the reason a social work referral is part of the medical plan, and the first thing to teach. Treating the pneumonia without addressing why he stopped simply schedules the next admission.
